item.title: Langfuse CLI v4 released with new commands and API versioning
item.description:
Langfuse CLI v4 released with new commands and API versioning

Langfuse has released a new CLI tool, @langfuse/cli, which allows users to interact with the Langfuse API directly from the command line. This new release includes updates to command aliases, input handling for complex JSON structures, and specific versioning rules for self-hosted versus cloud deployments.

📦 Package details

  • Package name: @langfuse/cli
  • Executable: langfuse
  • Legacy name: Previously published under langfuse-cli; the new name is recommended for all future use.

⚙️ Configuration and Host Selection

The CLI does not automatically read .env files. Users must manually configure API access and host selection. Host selection follows a specific priority order:

Priority Configuration Method
1 LANGFUSE_BASE_URL
2 LANGFUSE_HOST
3 EU default

To authenticate, users create a project API key pair under Project settings → API Keys.

🧩 Command and Input Features

  • Lossless input: --body-json and --body-file flags provide a lossless input path for nested objects, arrays, unions, and free-form JSON.
  • Pagination: The CLI can fetch every page of a paginated list, supporting both page- and cursor-based endpoints, with a maximum of 1000 items.
  • Aliases: OpenAPI tags and explicit route versions remain accepted aliases (e.g., scores-v3 list for the canonical scores list).
  • Schema: Verbose OpenAPI operationId values are available in api schema --json but are never required as CLI commands.

🌐 Availability and Versioning

  • V3 API Snapshots: Available on self-hosted deployments only.
  • Langfuse Cloud: Supports v4 and up.
  • Backward Compatibility: Users can use an API snapshot compatible with an older self-hosted deployment.

#Langfuse #CLI #API #DeveloperTools

Source: langfuse/langfuse-cli

item.title: Model Context Protocol Registry API Enters v0.1 API Freeze
item.description:
Model Context Protocol Registry API Enters v0.1 API Freeze

The community-driven Model Context Protocol (MCP) registry service has launched in preview and its Registry API (v0.1) has entered an API freeze.

🔍 Overview

  • The MCP registry provides MCP clients with a list of MCP servers, functioning like an app store for MCP servers.
  • The registry has launched in preview with an announcement blog post.
  • While the system is now more stable, this is still a preview release and breaking changes or data resets may occur.
  • A general availability (GA) release will follow later.

⚙️ Key details

  • For the next month or more, the API will remain stable with no breaking changes, allowing integrators to confidently implement support.
  • This freeze applies to v0.1 while development continues on v0.
  • This period will be used to validate the API in real-world integrations and gather feedback to shape v1 for general availability.
  • Publishing an MCP server does not happen through a pull request to the repository; adding a server.json, a server directory, or an entry in data/seed.json will not publish or list your server, even if the PR is merged.
  • Users must use the mcp-publisher CLI from their server’s own project instead.

🚀 Availability

  • The registry uses ko to build container images, and pre-built Docker images are automatically published to GitHub Container Registry.
  • Starting the registry at localhost:8080 with PostgreSQL uses ephemeral storage that resets each time containers are restarted.
  • By default, the registry seeds from the production API with a filtered subset of servers to keep startup fast.
  • The image does not bundle PostgreSQL, so users must run their own and point the registry at it via MCP_REGISTRY_DATABASE_URL.
  • Setup can be configured with environment variables in docker-compose.yml, and .env.example provides a reference.
  • Docker run commands are available for ghcr.io/modelcontextprotocol/registry:latest, :main, :v1.0.0, and :main-20250906-abc123d.

👥 Contributors

  • Radoslav (Rado) Dimitrov (Stacklok) [@rdimitrov] - WG Lead
  • Tadas Antanavicius (PulseMCP) [@tadasant]
  • Bob Dickinson (TeamSpark) [@BobDickinson]
  • Preeti (Pree) Dewani (Ravenmail) [@pree-dew]

💡 Collaboration

  • Multiple channels are used for collaboration as detailed on modelcontextprotocol.io/community/communication.

item.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models with updated pricing
item.description:
OpenAI introduces GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models with updated pricing

OpenAI has introduced two new frontier models: GPT-6.2 Astra, designed for the hardest projects, and GPT-6.2 Sol, an efficient and versatile model for everyday work. These models are now available via API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol, with support included in LLM 0.38.

🚀 Availability

The new models have been integrated into the OpenAI API and related developer tools:

  • Available in the API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol.
  • Support was shipped in LLM 0.38.
  • The models can be accessed using the Codex CLI and Codex desktop app with “Ultra” effort levels.

⚙️ Key details

Pricing for the new models reflects significant discounts compared to their predecessors. GPT-6.2 Astra is priced at 80% of the cost of the previous 6 Astra model, while GPT-6.2 Sol maintains the same pricing structure as previous Sol versions.

Model Input Price (per MTok) Output Price (per MTok) Cached Price (per MTok)
GPT-6.2 Astra $8 $40 $0.40
GPT-6.2 Sol $2 $10 Not specified

Performance and User Experience

  • Benchmarks: GPT-6.2 Astra is not scoring quite as high as Claude Fable 5.2 on various benchmarks.
  • Coding Tasks: In a specific three.js animation task prompting a mech to stomp around Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn, neither GPT-6.2 Astra nor Sol performed as well as Claude Fable 5.2 and Gemini 4 Carbon in morphing Yonkers into a big mech.
  • Communication Style: Users have reported that GPT-6.2 Astra’s communication style can be confusing. Theo Browne noted that the model can pull in subagents and manage them well but may ask users “weird internal implementation detail” questions they cannot understand, such as asking if a specific reviewer writes clips to 24_g521.mp4 or 24_p11.mp4 while working on a game level.

#OpenAI #GPT-6.2 #API #Pricing #Benchmarks

Source: GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol

item.title: Speaches provides an OpenAI-compatible API for speech-to-text and text-to-speech
item.description:
Speaches provides an OpenAI-compatible API for speech-to-text and text-to-speech

Speaches is an OpenAI API-compatible server that supports streaming transcription, translation, and speech generation.

🔍 Overview

  • The project aims to be the equivalent of Ollama, but specifically for TTS/STT models.
  • It is OpenAI API compatible, meaning all tools and SDKs that work with OpenAI’s API should work with speaches.
  • Supports GPU and CPU environments.
  • Deployable via Docker Compose or Docker.
  • Highly configurable.
  • Includes a Realtime API.

🧩 How it works

  • Speech-to-Text: Powered by faster-whisper.
  • Text-to-Speech: Uses piper and Kokoro models.
  • Streaming: Transcription is sent via SSE as the audio is transcribed; users do not need to wait for the audio to fully be transcribed before receiving it.
  • Dynamic Model Loading: Users specify which model to use in the request, and it is loaded automatically. The model is unloaded after a period of inactivity.

💡 Why it matters

Speaches enables specific audio-to-text and text-to-audio workflows:

  • Generate a spoken audio summary of a body of text (text in, audio out).
  • Perform sentiment analysis on a recording (audio in, text out).
  • Support async speech-to-speech interactions with a model (audio in, audio out).

#OpenAI #SpeechRecognition #TextToSpeech #Docker #API

Source: speaches-ai/speaches

item.title: LLM 0.37 addresses security vulnerabilities in API key handling
item.description:
LLM 0.37 addresses security vulnerabilities in API key handling

🔍 Overview

On 11th November 2026, a security update was released for LLM to address two vulnerabilities reported by Daniel de Araujo in GHSA-v9h7-jj4g-f862 and GHSA-r639-rr7r-x72w.

⚙️ Key details

The security issues involved the accidental transmission of configured OpenAI API keys to external providers when using OpenAI-compatible API endpoints. The report identified two specific scenarios where this exposure could occur:

  • When a key named by api_key_name had not been previously stored.
  • When a ‘responses: true’ model was executed with the ‘-o chat_completions 1’ flag.

🧩 How it works

LLM utilizes a mechanism known as ’extra-openai-models.yaml’ to facilitate the use of OpenAI-compatible API endpoints from other providers. This mechanism is now managed by the new ’llm openai endpoint add’ command introduced in version 0.37.

#LLM #Security #OpenAI #API

Source: Release: llm 0.37.2

item.title: Amazon Bedrock Adds Structured Output Support for Anthropic Claude Models
item.description:
Amazon Bedrock Adds Structured Output Support for Anthropic Claude Models

Amazon Bedrock now supports structured outputs for all Anthropic Claude models, enabling developers to receive schema-compliant JSON responses across both bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints.

🧩 How it works

Structured outputs use constrained decoding to enforce JSON schemas during token generation. This process shifts output formatting from probabilistic to deterministic, ensuring the model does not produce tokens that violate the defined schema.

Key mechanisms include:

Mechanism Function Use Case
JSON Schema output format Control response structure Data extraction, report generation, API responses
Strict tool use Validate tool parameters Agentic workflows, function calling, multi-step automation

⚙️ Key details

  • Compliance: Amazon Bedrock validates JSON schemas against the JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 subset.
  • Performance: The system compiles a grammar artifact for new schemas. These are cached for 24 hours per account to improve subsequent request speeds.
  • Efficiency: By constraining responses to only defined fields, output token counts are reduced, which can lower inference costs for high-volume workloads.
  • Implementation: On the bedrock-runtime endpoint, the schema is placed in output_config.format as a JSON object.
  • Tooling: On the bedrock-mantle endpoint, setting strict: true constrains tool inputs to match the provided schema exactly.

🚀 Availability

  • Endpoints: Supported on both bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle.
  • Inference: Works with batch inference for asynchronous processing.
  • Cross-Region: Supported on the bedrock-runtime endpoint for cross-Region inference without additional setup.
  • Real-time: Structured responses can be streamed as typed events.

💡 Why it matters

Structured outputs eliminate common issues such as JSON.parse() errors and parsing exceptions. Because responses are type-safe and required fields are guaranteed to be present, developers can build more reliable agentic workflows that interact with server-side tools.

#AmazonBedrock #AnthropicClaude #JSON #GenerativeAI #API

Source: Structured outputs for Anthropic Claude models on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Codex Pooler Introduced as Self-Hosted Gateway for Codex-Compatible Agents
item.description:
Codex Pooler Introduced as Self-Hosted Gateway for Codex-Compatible Agents

Codex Pooler is a self-hosted gateway designed to run Codex-compatible agents, tools, and automation using stable Pool API keys.

🔍 Overview

Codex Pooler allows operators to manage pools, accounts, API keys, saved resets, routing, request accounting, audit logs, and health. The system is designed so that operators do not store raw Codex secrets, bearer tokens, prompts, files, audio, or images.

🧩 How it works

Clients send OpenAI-compatible or Codex backend requests to the Codex Pooler. The system then selects an eligible account based on the following criteria:

  • Model support
  • Quota evidence
  • Limits
  • Session continuity
  • Routing policy
  • Health

⚙️ Key details

Feature Description
Stable Pool API keys Provides clients with one credential regardless of whether the Pool has one or several upstream accounts, avoiding the distribution of raw Codex account material.
Eligibility-aware routing Routes requests to accounts with matching health, session state, Pool policy, usable quota evidence, and compatible model support.
Codex backend compatibility Allows Codex-compatible clients to point at Codex Pooler while maintaining usage, compacting, and responses.

💡 Why it matters

  • Credential Isolation: It works with one upstream Codex account for client normalization, metadata-only operations, saved reset visibility, and credential isolation.
  • Scalability: Additional accounts can be added for routing and shared capacity across eligible accounts.
  • Stability: The Pool key remains stable even when capacity, reset policy, lifecycle state, and upstream assignments change.
  • Administrative Control: Instance owners maintain the global administration surface, while instance admins are restricted to their assigned Pools.

#Codex #API #AIagents #SelfHosted

Source: icoretech/codex-pooler

item.title: OpenRouter Model Routing and Provider Control Features
item.description:
OpenRouter Model Routing and Provider Control Features

OpenRouter provides an API endpoint that automatically handles fallbacks and selects the most cost-effective option for model requests.

⚙️ Key details

Because different providers use various serving software, optimizations, and settings, the same OpenRouter endpoint can result in requests that behave in different ways. These differences include:

  • Some providers lack vision capability for vision models.
  • The processing of the reasoning effort option can differ between providers.

🧩 How it works

Users have tools to manage how their requests are routed:

  • provider.only option: Allows users to control which specific provider is routed to.
  • /endpoints method: Returns a list of available providers for a specific model ID.

#OpenRouter #API #LLM #ModelRouting

Source: So you want to use OpenRouter?

item.title: OpenAI introduces ChatGPT Images 2.5
item.description:
OpenAI introduces ChatGPT Images 2.5

OpenAI has released ChatGPT Images 2.5, an update to image generation models that have been used for more than 3 billion images across ChatGPT Images and the GPT‑Image models in the API.

⚙️ Key details

This latest release includes several improvements:

  • Faster response times
  • Better ability to preserve subjects in reference photos
  • Improved instruction-following ability across multiple turns

🚀 Availability

Two new model IDs are available in the API:

Model ID Use Case
gpt-image-2.5-sunburst Workflows where editing precision matters most
gpt-image-2.5-flare Fast, high-quality everyday image generation

#OpenAI #ChatGPT #ImageGeneration #API
